thread:
jamie: quick follow-up from the RFC review: we sketched an "ingress-oblivious" proxy model that does minimal per-request state and relies on a compact handshake to enable streaming resume and safe retries. i have a few clarifying questions before we codify the API surface.

kate: thanks for starting this. can you recap the exact guarantees we want the handshake to provide vs what stays controller-only?

jamie: sure. handshake should give: short-lived session id (opaque), resume-token TTL, a minimal routing hint (model family + quantization tag), and a psuedo-idempotency nonce. proxy remains oblivious to model internals, only uses hints for fallback routing and capacity-typing.

mike: curious about the psuedo-idempotency nonce. why not full idempotency keys from clients? won't that complicate proxy caching?

jamie: two reasons: 1) we need something the proxy can validate cheaply without hitting control plane, 2) clients won't always supply idempotency keys for streaming requests. the nonce is locally verifiable (HMAC over session id + short counter) so proxy can dedupe transient dupes but doesn't have to be authoritative for long-term de-dup. full idempotency still handled at service tier.

nina: i worry about billing/duplication: if proxy dedupes and drops a retried request but the backend already charged tokens, metrics could diverge. how do we reconcile?

jamie: good call. plan is: proxy-level dedupe is best-effort and only covers obvious double-sends within the handshake TTL window. we emit an event with the candidate dedupe and let billing reconcile using downstream event stream + session id. fallback: if there's any ambiguity, proxy forwards and tags request with "X-RW-UNSURE-DEDUP".

ravi: what about streaming resume? if a client reconnects, we want to resume from last token. this means the proxy needs to accept resume-token and route to the same pool variant. but if proxy is oblivious, how does it know where to route?

jamie: resume-token encodes routing hint + checkpoint id. proxies use the routing hint to pick a compatible pool; they don't need exact model version. runtime provides compatibility rules: same family + quantization level is ok for resume, worst-case small mismatch triggers fallback to a restart and client-visible partial response.

mike: define "compatible" more concretely. some models differ in KV cache semantics. resuming into slightly different arch could corrupt decode. is that acceptable?

kate: we should be conservative: compatibility means identical generation kernels or an explicit resume compatibility tag published by runtime. handshake will carry "compat-v1" or "compat-none". if compat-none, proxy refuses resume and signals client to restart.

nina: signalling path? clients expect streamed errors or trailers. how do we surface a resume refusal so SDKs can automatically retry vs restart?

jamie: plan: proxy will inject a trailer: `resume-status: refused; reason=compat; advice=restart`. SDKs treat refused as non-idempotent restart. for transient issues (pool busy) proxy returns `resume-status: deferrable; retry-after=3s` and we keep the session TTL alive.

ravi: +1 to trailers. also agree on tagging uncertain dedupe. can we add a lightweight observability field: `X-RW-Session-Trace` that threads across logs for troubleshooting? make it a short base62 id.

ops-bot: deploy-check: ingress-handshake-spec v1 queued for staging. CI: 1 failing test (session ttl edge case).

kate: implementation detail — where do we store session ephemeral state? in-process LRU or sidecar? memory pressure on the proxy is real if we keep many ephemeral sessions for long-tail mobile clients.

jamie: initial approach: in-process bounded LRU with soft eviction and write-through to our fast key-value (memstore) for handoff. session TTL default 30s, extend on active stream chunks. eviction policy: evict oldest idle; when evicted, tag session as "stale" and proxies will return `resume-status: stale` instead of accepting resume.

mike: any thoughts on protecting the handshake from malicious clients who spam sessions? rate-limit by source IP + API key + exponential backoff. also allocate a small token-bucket per API key.

nina: security: HMAC keys for nonce validation live in KMS; proxy rotates cached HMAC keys every 24h. rotation must be backward compatible for 2 windows to allow graceful rollout.

ravi: edge-case: partial response billing if resume fails mid-stream. recommend we include `X-RW-Partial-Offset` in the resume-token metadata so billing and evals can align tokens counted vs emitted.

jamie: agreed. include offset and final-checksum in token. small snippet for handshake header we propose:

```
X-RW-Session: s=abcd1234;ttl=30
X-RW-Resume-Token: r=Zk9..;offset=512;compat=compat-v1
X-RW-Nonce: n=HMAC(...)
X-RW-Trace: t=bx9A
```

kate: love the explicit fields. one last thing: fallback routing when capacity constrained — proxy should be allowed to route to a lower-cost family (small-v2) but only for non-critical requests and with explicit `fallback-allowed` bit from the controller. and we MUST surface that to SDKs so UI can degrade gracefully.

jamie: recommended policy: fallback allowed only when client tier permits; proxy inserts `X-RW-Fallback: small-v2` header in response so SDK can render a degraded badge. also controller will log these events for SLO alerts.

mike: ok. i'd like an integration test that simulates resume into an incompatible pool and verifies the client sees `resume-status: refused` trailer and that metrics record a resume_failure with tags {reason:compat}.

ops-bot: staging deploy patched, integration tests queued. CI: 0 new failures after fix. :rocket:

nina: sounds good. i'll draft a compact handshake spec doc from this thread and add a small state machine diagram. anyone want to own the first pass of the SDK handling logic for refused/deferrable/stale?

ravi: i'll take SDK handling for JS + Python. mike, can you own proxy LRU implementation?

mike: yep. i'll open a PR for the LRU plus memstore write-through.

jamie: thanks all — i'll capture decisions and update the RFC: handshake fields, compat semantics, ttl, dedupe best-effort, observability tags, fallback policy. leaving this open for any final nits for 24h. :thumbsup:
